newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: APEC energy ministers to meet in Canada Aug 26, 27.
newsitem.headline: APEC energy ministers to meet in Canada Aug 26, 27.

text.p: Energy ministers from the APEC forum are expected to address issues ranging from market liberalisation to business standards when they meet in Canada in August, energy officials in Asia said.
APEC (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation) officials said on Friday the meeting will take place in Edmonton, Alberta on August 26 and 27.
An energy business meeting and energy youth programme are scheduled in the four days before the ministerial gathering.
APEC members in Asia said they expected the meeting to address various issues, including energy market liberalisation and energy business standards, exchange of information and views.
"It's likely that the energy sector will be pushed as a sector for early voluntary liberalisation," Philippine assistant secretary of energy Cyril del Callar said.

The gathering -- including Pacific rim countries and North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) members the United States, Canada and Mexico -- will represent the biggest crude consuming block on earth.
Asia consumes around 18 million barrels per day and is expected to surpass North America's consumption rates of 20.7 million barrels per day by the turn of the century.
North America already operates a relatively open energy sector, while Asian countries are at various levels of liberalisation.

APEC groups the United States, Canada, Mexico, Chile, China, Japan, Australia, Brunei, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan and Thialand.
